signal: Prove launched a Global Identity Graph and a Verified Agent solution for agentic commerce in October 2025, expanding its product footprint

email.body1:
Patrick, saw Prove launched its Global Identity Graph and a Verified Agent solution for agentic commerce this past October.

New product lines like that flood the funnel with signals faster than they can be turned into action. Our AI SDR closes that signal-to-action latency, researching, writing, and following up autonomously: 3-5x more meetings per rep, no new hires.

I built a personalized signal play for Prove off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Patrick, quick follow-up for Prove.

Launching new lines usually means signals piling up faster than reps can act on them. As RevOps, you feel that latency first, and it's hard to prove measurable lift when follow-up is the bottleneck.

Want 15 minutes? I'll walk you through a teardown of your current outbound, three things I'd change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Patrick, last bit of proof for Prove.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Prove's reply rate likely compares to other identity and fintech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Patrick, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If tightening signal-to-action without adding headcount isn't a priority while the new lines ramp, no problem at all. Timing is everything around launches, and that stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a RevOps motion? I'll tailor it to Prove either way.
